title: Is This Call Really From Medicare?
youtube_title: Medicare Open Enrollment Scams: How to Spot a Fake Call | Fix It Friday
next: Next Friday: another fix from your comments
description: Medicare Open Enrollment runs October 15 to December 7, and scammers know it. Kip and Bub show the warning signs of a fake Medicare call, text or letter, what Medicare will never ask for, how to avoid fake Medicare ads in search results, and the safe way to check: hang up and call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) yourself.

scenes.say: Your phone rings. The caller says they're from Medicare, and you need to act today or lose your coverage. Is it real?
It's Fix It Friday. Today: is this call really from Medicare?
Medicare Open Enrollment runs from October fifteenth to December seventh. It's a real time to review your plan. But it's also the busiest season of the year for scammers.
Here are the warning signs. They rush you. They ask for your Medicare number. They offer a free gift or a new card. Or they threaten that you'll lose your coverage.
Remember this one rule. Medicare won't call you out of the blue asking for your Medicare number or your bank details. Treat your Medicare number like a credit card.
And caller ID can lie. Scammers can make any name or number show up on your screen, even one that says Medicare.
So what do you do? Hang up. Then call Medicare yourself at one, eight hundred, Medicare. That's one, eight hundred, six three three, four two two seven. If the call was real, they'll know.
The same goes for texts, emails and letters that look official. Don't tap the link or call the number in the message. Use the number on your Medicare card instead.
Searching online for Medicare help? Watch the top results. Scammers pay for ads that look like Medicare. Skip anything marked Sponsored, and type Medicare dot gov yourself.
Want real help choosing a plan? Every state has a free Medicare counseling program, often called SHIP. They don't sell anything, and they won't rush you.
So: slow down, guard your Medicare number, don't trust caller ID, and hang up and call Medicare yourself.
Share this with someone on Medicare. It could save them a lot of trouble. Got a tech problem you want fixed? Leave it in the comments. See you next Friday.
